credit_spreads._note: Minimum net credit as a fraction of strike width. Shipped at 0.20. HISTORY, kept because the round trip is the useful part: tightened 0.20 -> 0.30 on 2026-08-13 on the argument that the scan board demanded a 76-79% win rate while the book delivers 66.4%, then REVERTED to 0.20 the same day when that argument was measured and failed. Two errors in it: (1) it compared different populations - 76-79% described scan candidates at credit/width ~0.21-0.34, while the 66.4% came from logged trades at median credit/width 0.475, so the filter was never what selected them; (2) it used the HOLD-TO-EXPIRY identity 1-r, which at credit/width 0.475 says 52.5% against a MEASURED managed requirement of 50.9% - a 1.6pp gap, so the identity was fine and its application was not. Under the exits actually used (config.exit_rules.spread, TP 0.5 / SL -1.0), Bull Put requires 50.9% and delivers 66.4%, clearing its bar by 15.6pp over 131 closed trades. The families that FAIL their own breakeven are Bear Call (needs 66.7%, delivers 59.3%) and Iron Condor (needs 60.1%, delivers 50.0%) - not bull puts, and not a credit-to-width problem. Judge a credit structure against the MANAGED required rate for its family, not against 1-credit/width. Mirrors filters.iron_condor.min_credit_to_width - keep the two in step.

auto_log._max_capital_at_risk_note: Dollars a single position may tie up before the LEDGER refuses to log it. As of 2026-08-14 this is the SCHEDULER's budget only: SIX interactive modes ask for their own budget per scan and default to no limit, and the number they choose is what binds their logging: DISCOVER, MY LIST, TICKER, SELL, SPREADS, IRON. Every other interactive path is still bound by THIS value - the ALL/Budget scan (which already asks a per-CONTRACT budget, a different quantity), LOTTERY, SQUEEZE, and a bare ticker typed straight at the menu. A run that is never asked has not chosen no limit. The value is unchanged at 4000. It exists because the feeder had no limit at all and was logging $27k and $83k positions, and because the split it enables is what makes the book readable - inside the budget +$3,283 (n=247), above it -$19,741 (n=160), with Long Call going -$21,718 to +$183 once the unaffordable rows are excluded. Note this cap also flatlines the short-put line: a cash-secured put's risk is strike x 100, so AVGO at $34,680 and BA at $20,410 are refused every day and the window still exits rc=0. Raise it or set it null to change that, deliberately. null disables it; allow_unaffordable=True bypasses it for one trade.
auto_log._dedup_window_days_note: Days an auto-logged contract blocks a second AUTO-LOG of the same (ticker, strategy, strike, expiration). The per-day dedup only sees today, so a catch-up replay re-logs the same contract the next morning at a drifted price and double-counts one decision. Manual log_trade calls are never gated by this. 0 or null disables it.
auto_log._max_friction_to_credit_note: Refuse to auto-log a CREDIT trade whose round-trip friction exceeds this fraction of the credit received. TIGHTENED 0.50 -> 0.25 on 2026-08-06: the allocation backtest measured the MEDIAN crossing cost at exactly 50% of credit ($90 at mid, $45 received, over 400 real trades), so a 0.50 ceiling admitted roughly half of all candidates - and those are the ones that lose. Restricting the universe to names whose spreads are 3.6% of mid rather than 16-21% moved the same strategy from -6.76% to -0.64% return on capital (t=-17.84, n=10,363), the largest single effect measured anywhere in this system. This filter only REFUSES trades, never adds them, and is the conservative direction. Revert via config.bak.20260806-224238-friction.json. Above 1.0 the trade cannot profit at any win rate. Measured 2026-07-31: 31 of 188 logged short-premium trades were above 1.0 — micro-spreads with $57 median capital at risk against ~$65 of spread — and excluding those above 0.50 moved the family's median return on risk from +12.6% to +28.1%. This is the mirror of max_capital_at_risk: that refuses positions too LARGE for the account, this refuses positions too SMALL to survive their own market. null disables it; allow_untradeable=True bypasses it for a deliberate manual entry.
auto_log._paper_only_strategies_note: Strategies logged as paper_only=1, i.e. kept OUT of any validation cohort. NOW EMPTY. A strategy in NEITHER allowed_strategies NOR this list is DROPPED by apply_auto_log_allowlist and never auto-logged at all — emptying this is therefore how a strategy is switched off. 2026-08-13: Iron Condor removed, stopping its auto-log. It needs a 60.1% win rate under the exits actually used and has delivered 50.0% over 142 closed trades (-10.1pp); Bear Call is -7.4pp and had already stopped logging on 2026-07-31. 2026-08-01: Bull Put, Bear Call and Short Put were removed from this list by operator decision so the short-premium gate's cohort could authorise capital, and the 285 historical rows were flipped to paper_only=0 (backup: backups/paper_trades.db.bak.20260801-223429). NOTE the side effect, which was probably not intended: because none of the three was added to allowed_strategies, all three stopped being auto-logged entirely that day. 2026-08-18: that side effect was REVERSED for Bull Put only, by adding it to allowed_strategies — it needs 50.9% under the exits actually used and has delivered 66.4% over 131 closed trades (+$5,315), the only line in the book that clears its own bar. Bear Call (-7.4pp) and Short Put (-$8,278 over 109 closed) were switched off by accident but stay off on their evidence. Note that allowed_strategies, not this list, is where a credit strategy belongs: paper_only=1 would log it into permanent quarantine, invisible to the short-premium gate. The cohort DTE floor does NOT apply to it — see _HORIZON_GUARDED_STRATEGIES in options_screener.py, since 119 of 132 historical Bull Puts sit below the 30-DTE floor and the floor is long-premium reasoning. NOTE ALSO that paper_only means two different things in this ledger: strategy-selection quarantine (this list) and DTE-contamination marking on Long Call/Long Put rows. 2026-08-19: LONG CALL REMOVED from allowed_strategies, leaving Bull Put as the only auto-logged strategy. Reason: audited on the ledger with position sizing removed. Every row carries quantity = 1.0, so as-sized P&L mostly describes option premiums rather than picks; equal-weighted over 295 closed Long Calls the profit factor is 1.035 with a 95% bootstrap CI of [0.783, 1.335], an interval containing 1, so no edge is detectable. The post-repair cohort is the same result at full volume: 25 closed, -$9,890, 24% win, PF 0.098. That cohort was audited for a defect and none was found - exit prices reconcile against chain_archive.db which the ledger never reads (QQQ recorded 6.28 against 6.43, 6.80 against 6.87), the -50% stop is implemented correctly, and the underlying moved against the position in 12 of 16 measurable cases; the trades simply lost. Long Call is NOT in paper_only_strategies, because that list still LOGS the trade and merely quarantines it. It keeps being scanned and recorded to data/candidates.db, whose forward marks now cover structures too, so the strategy keeps producing evidence without consuming book capital - restore it here if that evidence turns. Note the consequence: the ds/ss/ics scheduler windows can now log nothing at all, and only sps can produce an entry, so a silent day is expected rather than a broken gate.

ai_scoring._note: false = no AI ranking on any run (same as --no-ai everywhere), incl. interactive. Set true to re-enable the LLM rerank.

paper_trading._broker: Wealthsimple (Ontario, CAD account). Verified against their published fee schedule 2026-07-29.
paper_trading._commission_note: Wealthsimple charges US$0 commission and US$0 per-contract fee on equity and ETF options, every tier. The previous 0.65 was a US-retail assumption and overstated cost on every logged trade. INDEX options are NOT free: SPX/SPXW and VIX are US$1/contract, RUT US$0.50, XSP US$0.25 — this field does not model those, so treat index-option results as understated.
paper_trading._fx_note: USD account ACTIVE as of 2026-07-31 (operator confirmed the USD trading subscription), so there is NO per-trade CAD->USD conversion spread: this is 0.0 rather than the 1.5% a CAD account pays below US$10k of conversions. The subscription costs US$10/month, which is a FIXED cost and therefore not modelled per trade — it does not belong in a per-trade friction number, but it is real and does not shrink with activity. Revert to 0.015 if the subscription lapses; the tiering below it was 1.5% under US$10k, 1.0% to $25k, 0.5% to $100k, 0% above.
paper_trading._exercise_note: Assignment US$0 and auto-exercise US$0, so letting a spread expire or be assigned is free. EARLY exercise is US$45, as is a do-not-exercise instruction — both are large against a $122 median credit and are not modelled here.

crypto._auto_log_enabled_note: OFF since 2026-08-18. The crypto auto-logger has no strategy allowlist — pick_winner takes the single highest top-of-bucket score per currency, and Long Put won 98 of 98 decisions all-time while being the only losing strategy in the crypto book: -$3,186 over 52 closed at 28.8%, against Bear Call +$2,277, Long Call +$3,114, Calendar Put +$1,377. The book's +$3,582 comes entirely from the 11 trades the auto-logger did NOT choose; the auto-logged cohort alone is -$2,400 at 34.6%, and deteriorating (2026-07 was 0-for-4 at -$3,762, 2026-08 20% at -$734). Consistent with the measured crypto VRP: BTC short premium clears the cost wall, long premium does not. This switch is the FIRST check in run_currency, before any scan or ledger access, so nothing is fetched and nothing can be written while it is false. It stops NEW entries only — the crypto exit enforcer is a separate LaunchAgent and still manages the 2 open Long Puts. NOT a verdict on Bear Call: its 9 wins are all BTC inside 2026-05-04..2026-06-25, one regime, and 100% over n=9 is not an edge estimate. Re-enable only alongside a selection rule that does not let one score column monopolise the board.

leverage_selector._note: funding_rate_daily null => derived LIVE each scan from the fetched short rate (^IRX) + carry_spread_annual; set a positive number only to pin a manual override. maintenance_margin and max_leverage are venue constants.
leverage_selector.venues_note: synthetic equity perps via USDC/USDT from a Phantom wallet: gTrade (Base/Arbitrum), xStocks tokenized equities (Solana) collateralised on Kamino, Ostium RWA perps (Arbitrum)

data_providers._note: Free Finnhub key (finnhub.io/register) enables reliable earnings dates + dividend yields; falls back to yfinance when blank. Env FINNHUB_API_KEY overrides this.

gate._note: Phase-1 gate rule. version 2 is the signed redesign (docs/GATE_REDESIGN_SPEC.md, operator sign-off 2026-07-31): decides on the SPEARMAN rank IC via posterior bands at EFFECTIVE n, with a bounded EXTEND. version 1 is the superseded Pearson/p-value rule, kept runnable so its verdict can still be computed; both are reported on every checkpoint regardless of which governs.
gate._extensions_used_note: SEED ONLY as of 2026-08-01 — do not expect editing this to change a verdict. How many 2-week EXTENDs have been granted under v2; at 2 the gate must resolve READY or STOP rather than extending again, the terminal condition v1 lacked. This used to say 'increment when an EXTEND is acted on', which nobody did and nobody could do correctly, because an integer records how many extensions were granted but never when one STARTED — so no code could tell whether two weeks had elapsed, and a daily checkpoint reprinted 'extension 1 of 2' indefinitely. The clock now lives in status/gate_extensions.json and is advanced by the calendar; these two fields seed it on first run and are ignored thereafter. See src/gate_extensions.py.
gate._short_premium_note: The short-premium gate (spec section 2.4) runs beside the Long Call gate every checkpoint. Arm A (family viability, clustered-bootstrap posterior on the median net return-on-risk) is the arm that would authorise capital; Arm B (rank IC) only decides whether live trading would use the scorer to pick contracts. 2026-08-01: the operator ruled on the paper_only question and PROMOTED the family, so this cohort is validation evidence rather than reporting — but nothing is armed by it. What authorises the execution pipeline is authorising_gate below, and the binding caveat is unchanged: the window contains no volatility shock, so the tail this family fails on has never been observed.
gate._authorising_gate_note: Which gate the Phase-3 execution pipeline reads to decide ARMED vs DISARMED. 'long_call' is the historical wiring; it resolved STOP. 'short_premium' would read Arm A of the short-premium gate instead, which reads READY — deliberately NOT selected: pointing the pipeline at the arm that says yes is a real-money decision, and it is not implied by the promotion that made the cohort readable. Changing this is necessary but not sufficient to trade; live_execution.enabled is a separate switch.
